source_snapshot.procedure_direct_xlsx: 【Before Test】 1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition. 2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.). 【During Test】 1. Bios Setting EDKII Menu -> Socket Configuration -> Processor Configuration -> Lock Chipset -> Disabled EDKII Menu -> Socket Configuration -> Processor Configuration -> MSR Lock Control -> Disabled EDKII Menu -> Socket Configuration -> IIO Configuration -> IIO DFX Configuration -> EV DFX features -> Enabled EDKII Menu -> Socket Configuration -> IIO Configuration -> IIO DFX Configuration -> Disable BIOS Done -> [‘X’] EDKII Menu -> Platform Configuration -> System Event Log -> Error Injection Settings -> WHEA Error Injection Support -> Enabled EDKII Menu -> Platform Configuration -> System Event Log -> Error Injection Settings -> Whea PCIE Error Injection Action Table -> Enabled 2. Deploy Intel ITP environment. 3. Boot SUT into shell 4. Execute Intel Cscripts on client 5. Using folling command >>>itp.log("C:\Test.log") >>>halt() >>>ei.injectIERR(socket) >>>go 【After Test】 1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders. 2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
source_snapshot.criteria_direct_xlsx: 1. System should crash and hang but reboot eventually 2. BMC error log should record CPU Catastrophic Error been detected 3. Front Panel fault Light will Light if there is one 4. uEFI SEL Log will show upi fatal error once you recover the system and boot into SEL log. 5. If there is a LCD Panel, CPU Over Temp error information will be displayed with details of affected CPU
source_snapshot.deepseek_direct_xlsx: PARTIAL | -- Socket 0~N (Intel IERR on Socket 0~N error injection): requires CScripts/EDKII unlock (Lock Chipset=Disable, MSR Lock Control=Disable, EV DFX Features=Enable, WHEA Error Injection Support=Enable) + the user/FAE to drive the Cscript/error-injection harness for this exact pattern. Agent captures the post-injection evidence with sshpass -p "$DUT_PASS" ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no $DUT_USER@$DUT_IP "dmesg -T 2>&1 | tail -180 | grep -iE 'IERR|internal.error|machine.check|MCE_'; echo __IERR_on_Socket_0~N; ipmitool sel elist 2>&1 | tail -40 2>&1".

disposition_reason: The explicit socket parameter makes target validation possible, but only if Intel's logical socket numbering is bound to the physical CPU before halt. IERR, UPI fatal and over-temperature are different event domains; a platform may intentionally translate them, yet the source provides no event-map evidence. During the expected crash the management controller and independent console, not SSH reachability, must anchor timing and fault identity. Because the missing package contract, mapping and timers are obtainable readiness inputs, the safe classification is REQUIRES PACKAGE / USER CONFIRMATION with execution withheld until the conflicting oracle is approved. test_case.purpose: Inject an Intel internal CPU error into each approved socket and confirm that the platform follows the specified catastrophic crash/reboot path while identifying the affected CPU consistently in OS, BMC, UEFI and physical displays.
required_package: Board/CPU socket map and supported ITP/CScripts package/version/hash
Authoritative IERR/internal-error, BMC catastrophic and UEFI event signatures
Maximum crash/hang and autonomous-reboot intervals with permitted recovery transitions
Front-panel/LCD applicability and correct affected-CPU message
Post-recovery health and BIOS restoration checklist
test_case.test_command: A qualified FAE/operator on an isolated SUT enables the exact EDKII settings, validates the numeric socket against the physical CPU, performs one approved `injectIERR(socket)` call, timestamps the intentional outage independently, waits the authorized autonomous-reboot window, collects IERR/catastrophic evidence after recovery, observes indicators and restores debug settings.
test_case.expected_result: 1. System should crash and hang but reboot eventually 2. BMC error log should record CPU Catastrophic Error been detected 3. Front Panel fault Light will Light if there is one 4. uEFI SEL Log will show upi fatal error once you recover the system and boot into SEL log. 5. If there is a LCD Panel, CPU Over Temp error information will be displayed with details of affected CPU
test_case.pass_fail_basis: No executable PASS verdict exists yet for Socket 0~N. The protected Criteria is `1. System should crash and hang but reboot eventually 2. Front Panel fault Light will Light if there is one 4. uEFI SEL Log will show upi fatal error once you recover the system and boot into SEL log. 5. If there is a LCD Panel, CPU Over Temp error information will be displayed with details of affected CPU`; it becomes enforceable only after resolving: Resolve Reliability row 11 Wistron-System RAS-00731-V003: approve CPU socket mapping, Intel ITP/CScripts version/hash and `injectIERR(socket)` semantics; define maximum crash/hang and autonomous-reboot timing, permitted recovery and BIOS restoration; specify exact IERR/internal-error, BMC/UEFI and front-panel evidence; and explain/correct the UPI-fatal UEFI and CPU Over Temp LCD criteria for an IERR stimulus.
safety_gate: Dedicated idle SUT, stable power, independent recovery console and explicit crash approval
Preserve pre-existing logs; do not clear evidence
Verify numeric socket identity before one injection
Do not power-cycle inside the protected reboot window and never automatically retry
Escalate wrong target, thermal/power anomaly, exceeded timeout, no boot or inconsistent evidence
expected_evidence: Harness hash, mapped socket argument and complete ITP transcript
Independent crash/hang/autonomous-reboot and any manual-recovery timeline
IERR/internal-error OS/console record, BMC catastrophic SEL and corrected recovered UEFI event
Front-panel/LCD affected-CPU evidence, BIOS restoration, health result and engineer verdict
test_case.recovery: Package and operator gates make a controlled future run possible; they do not authorize autonomous crash injection. Missing readiness yields a BLOCKED run, not DUT FAIL.

source_conflict.reason: The stimulus is CPU IERR, but Criteria demand a UEFI UPI fatal record and an LCD CPU Over Temp message without defining the platform event mapping. `Reboot eventually` also lacks a timeout and recovery boundary.

blocked.reason: Execution remains blocked by the case-specific vendor semantics, isolation and recovery listed in pending.remaining_project_configuration.
